720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.overview: The first part of Heath Pedigo's white belt curriculum from Pedigo Submission Fighting, a gym known for its record with white and blue belt competitors. Stripe 1 covers how a match starts and the first things a white belt needs: dealing with the standing exchange by pulling closed guard or sitting guard, attacking from closed guard (controlling posture, getting the arm across the centreline, attacking their structure), first submissions (sweep to mount or armbar, the armbar from bottom), and guard retention (sitting versus standing retention, re-guarding with a double lapel grip, dealing with pant grips). Heath troubleshoots with real white belt students as they learn.
720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.for: White belts, or coaches looking for a structured beginner syllabus.
key: Starting the match: pulling closed guard or sitting guard
Closed guard posture control and attacks

720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.overview: Stripe 2 of Heath Pedigo's white belt curriculum moves to top play. It starts with simple takedowns (the collar drag, a snatch single with a knee tap finish), then passing (the windshield wiper pass, the 'crotch killer', just standing up), then pinning and half guard passing (spreading the legs, stapling the arm from side control, 'the squeeze', pinning the shin to pass half guard). It finishes with knee on belly, scoring mount and a safer, faster back take.
720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.for: White belts building their first top game.
key: Collar drag and snatch single takedowns
Side control pins and half guard passing
Knee on belly, mount and back takes

720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.overview: Stripe 3 builds a passing system and top submissions. Outside passing comes first (kicking off De La Riva hooks, pop-push-grab, the U grip), then inside passing (double-under and stack passes). The second half covers submissions from top: americana, north-south choke, kimura with a pressure grip break, step-over triangle, two-handed brabo choke, cross collar punch choke, americana to armbar from mount, and the triangle when they break the armbar grip.
720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.for: White belts who can get on top but struggle to pass or finish.
key: Outside passing against De La Riva

720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.overview: Stripe 4 completes the white belt curriculum with offence from guard and key defences. It covers armbar mechanics from guard, the 'daisy sweep', the scissor sweep (called 'two knives'), setting up and finishing the triangle, the kimura with grip breaks and the kimura sweep, a showcase armbar, the short hook sweep and a simple foot lock. The last volume covers defence: the hitchhiker escape from the armbar (and how to stop it from top) and guillotine defence.
720p - The Daisy Fresh Curriculum White.for: White belts building an attacking guard.
key: Armbar, triangle and kimura from guard

[ CourseWikia.com ] BJJ Fanatics - Tacti.overview: Neil Melanson, a catch wrestling and MMA grappling coach, shows his system for turning the turtle from a defensive shell into an attacking position. Over eight volumes (about 9 hours) he covers body position and wrist control from turtle, then a large set of reversals and takedowns from the bottom: sweep singles, low singles, ankle picks, snap downs, front chokes and 2-on-1 arm drags. Later volumes cover standing up and sitting out, Granby and near-arm rolls, a long kimura sequence from turtle (including the sankaku), and finally how to shake off a back attacker who has one or two hooks or a power half nelson.
[ CourseWikia.com ] BJJ Fanatics - Tacti.for: Anyone who ends up in turtle, especially no-gi and MMA grapplers with a wrestling bent.
key: Turtle body position and wrist control
Sweep single, low single and ankle pick reversals
Escaping hooks and the power half

Adam Wardziński Pins And Dominant Positi.overview: Gi Super Grand Slam champion Adam Wardziński teaches escapes from the four major pins, one volume each: mount (principles, removing grapevines, digging and collecting the leg), side control (shrimp escape, near- and far-side underhook escapes, dealing with the crossface), turtle (Peterson roll, Granby roll, escaping to single leg X) and back control (escaping to standing, baiting the back take, sliding the hips down while preventing mount).
Adam Wardziński Pins And Dominant Positi.for: Gi players at any level who get stuck under heavy pressure.
key: Side control escapes and beating the crossface
Turtle rolls and escape to single leg X

Adele Fornarino Overhook From Everywhere.overview: Two-time ADCC champion Adele Fornarino shows how she uses the overhook throughout her game. Volume 1 covers holding the overhook and pairing it with a knee shield half guard. Volume 2 covers the clam sweep, chopstick guard, triangles (including a version for less flexible people) and wrestle-ups. Volume 3 links the knee shield with half butterfly for triangles, armbars and butterfly hook sweeps. Volume 4 covers the overhook from standing: uchi mata, ankle pick and the flying triangle.
Adele Fornarino Overhook From Everywhere.for: No-gi players who want the overhook as an attacking tool from the bottom and standing.
key: Holding the overhook with a knee shield
Overhook throws and the flying triangle from standing
